members.name: momentum_reversion_switch_v1
members.thesis: Intraday markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. During high-ADX periods (ADX(14) > 25), trend-following via EMA crossover outperforms. During low-ADX periods (ADX(14) < 18), Bollinger Band mean-reversion dominates. The inefficiency arises because most strategies are static —
entry_long: MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
entry_short: MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap
members.exit_target: MOMENTUM: 50 bps from entry; REVERSION: close crosses BB_mid (SMA(close,20))
filters: No filter — strategy is regime-adaptive by design
No entries in first 5 min (09:15-09:20) or after 15:00 IST
Stock must have traded > 500 shares in last 5 bars
None — strategy adapts to both trending and ranging
weaknesses: ADX(14) on 1-min bars takes ~28 bars to stabilize, losing the first 30 minutes of trading session to indicator warm-up
Regime classification in the ADX 18-25 'dead zone' is ambiguous — neither sub-strategy performs well, leading to whipsaws
Switching cost: each regime transition requires closing existing position and potentially reversing, doubling transaction costs during choppy transitions
members.prior_art: Ang & Timmermann (2012) regime-switching models; Kole & van Dijk (2017) on Markov-switching for trading; ADX regime classification is common in technical analysis literature

members.name: momentum_reversal_regime_switch_v1
members.thesis: Markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. This strategy uses ADX to detect the regime and switches between trend-following (ADX > 25) and mean-reversion (ADX < 18) approaches. In trending regimes: buy pullbacks to EMA(20). In range-bound regimes: fade VWAP extremes. The key insi
entry_long: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close > ema_20 AND low touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 > 40 AND close > vwap
entry_short: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close < ema_20 AND high touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 < 60 AND close < vwap
filters: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
ADX is the regime filter itself
weaknesses: ADX dead zone (18-25) means no trading during transitions — but transitions are where regime is most unclear
ADX on 1-min is slow to react — regime may have shifted before ADX reflects it
Two separate strategy logics increase complexity and parameter count (overfitting risk)
members.prior_art: Regime-switching models — Hamilton (1989). Practical implementation with ADX as regime proxy.

members.name: vol_regime_adaptive_v1
members.thesis: Intraday market behavior differs fundamentally across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes (ATR percentile < 30), mean-reversion dominates because moves are small and revert quickly. In high-vol regimes (ATR percentile > 70), momentum dominates because large moves carry information and attract ord
entry_long: LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap (mean-reversion buy)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum buy)
entry_short: LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap (mean-reversion sell)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum sell)
filters: India VIX < 28; adjust regime thresholds if VIX > 22 (shift ATR percentile buckets up by 10)
HIGH-VOL entries require volume > 2x SMA(volume,20); LOW-VOL has no additional volume filter
HIGH-VOL: NIFTY trend must agree; LOW-VOL: no trend filter
Bid-ask spread < 5 bps in LOW-VOL; < 8 bps in HIGH-VOL (wider spreads acceptable)
weaknesses: Medium-vol regime (30-70th percentile of ATR) accounts for ~40% of the time, during which the strategy is flat — significant opportunity cost and underutilization of capital
Regime transitions from LOW to HIGH can be abrupt (e.g., sudden news) — the 10-bar stability requirement causes the strategy to miss the most profitable initial bars of a vol spike
BB(20, 1.5) in low-vol regime uses narrow bands (1.5 sigma vs standard 2.0) — more signals but also more false signals in low-vol environments where noise dominates
members.prior_art: Volatility regime-switching in Ang & Chen (2002); ATR-based position sizing (Van Tharp); volatility clustering (Mandelbrot); regime-conditional mean-reversion/momentum widely discussed in quant litera
